outputs.exact_statement:
For every multiplier $W$ as above, the Banach space $X_W$ is infinite dimensional and has no equivalent AUC norm. For the exponential and Gaussian-square laws, the inherited norms satisfy $$\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\mathrm{exp}}}(t)
 &\ge \frac{7t}{30}c(10/t)>0 &&(t>0),\label{eq:main-exp}\\
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\mathrm{sq}}}(t)
 &\ge\frac{\mathbb P\bigl(|G|\ge4\sqrt2(2+\sqrt2)/t\bigr)}{8}>0
 &&(t>0),\label{eq:main-sq24}\\
 \widehat\delta_{X_{\mathrm{sq}}}(t)
 &\ge\frac{\mathbb P\bigl(|G|\ge8\sqrt6/t\bigr)}{4}>0
 &&(t>0).\label{eq:main-sq12}
\end{aligned}$$

Fix $t>0$ and nonnegative constants $A,B$. Suppose that, for every finite predecessor-closed $T$, every $u\in E_T$, and every finite-product combination $y\in F_T$, $$M_t(u,y)\ge A\lVert y\rVert_1-B\lVert u\rVert_1.$$ Then this inequality holds for all $y\in F_T$, and $$\widehat\delta_{X_W}(t)\ge\max\{0,A-B\}.$$

The excess estimate also permits a direct passage using a fixed positive approximation tolerance, rather than letting the center error tend to zero as in Lemma 3. Fix $t>0$, a finite predecessor-closed subtree $T$ containing the root, $u\in E_T$, and a finite-product combination $y\in F_T$. If $\lVert u\rVert_1\le2$ and $\lVert y\rVert_1\ge9/10$, then $\mathbb E\sigma\ge3/10$. On $A=\{|u|\le10\sigma\}$, at least $1/10$ of the expected coefficient size remains, because $\mathbb E(\sigma\mathbf1_{A^c})\le1/5$. Consequently [prob:exponential-excess], with $K=10/t$, gives $$M_t(u,y)\ge \frac t{10}c(10/t).$$ Finite-tail approximation extends this last bound to every $y\in F_T$ with $\lVert y\rVert_1\ge1$. Put $L_t=t c(10/t)/10$. Approximating a unit center with error less than $\min\{1,L_t/4\}$ ensures $\lVert u\rVert_1<2$ and loses less than $L_t/2$ by [prob:continuity]. Thus this passage gives the weaker estimate $\widehat\delta_{X_{\mathrm{exp}}}(t)\ge t c(10/t)/20$ for every $t>0$ directly, without using the affine conclusion of Lemma 3.
